I am an old man, sixty-seven years, farming this sorghum plot like I have done for many seasons. The land is mine, so I put my manure from the goats and few cattle on it every year — that helps small. I will buy one bag of urea if the cash is there from last harvest, and spread it carefully on the sorghum when it is knee-high. I keep my own seed from last year because the local sorghum knows this soil and the short rains we get here in the North East. I intercrop with cowpea like always, and my sons help me when they are around.
